idiom_name: hand-written order_load()/order_save() over a C DB API (sqlite3, libpq)
implementation_notes: C has no mapper framework, so the parent's mapper is a pair of functions - order_load() and order_save() - whose structs and SQL own the order_line rows; the child struct exists only inside the parent aggregate and never gets lookup or save functions of its own. Saving replaces the whole line set (DELETE then INSERT) inside one transaction, and the child table's foreign key is declared with ON DELETE CASCADE so deleting the parent removes the lines. The classic structure is not merely justified here but the only option, unless the mapper is generated by an external code generator.
pitfalls: PRAGMA foreign_keys is per-connection and off by default in SQLite, so ON DELETE CASCADE only fires if it was enabled on that connection.
Without BEGIN/COMMIT around delete and insert there is a window where the parent exists without its lines - and a crash mid-save leaves orphans.
The line array's memory belongs to the parent struct; freeing the parent must free the lines too, or use a flexible array member / a single arena.
